sentences.text: Latoplatecarpus was an extinct genus of mosasaur, a family of large marine reptiles. It belonged to the subfamily Plioplatecarpinae and the tribe Plioplatecarpini. This medium-sized aquatic predator reached lengths of 5 to 6 meters.

A study of materials from the Campanian Rybushka Formation in Russia identified Latoplatecarpus as the only identifiable plioplatecarpine genus in that location. This discovery shows the genus had a significantly wider geographic and stratigraphic distribution than previously known.

The genus was named by Konishi and Caldwell in 2011. The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — was collected from the Pembina Member of the Pierre Shale in southern Manitoba, dating to about 80.5 million years ago. It consists of a nearly complete skull with the mandible and dentary, plus a partial postcranial skeleton.

Fossils of Latoplatecarpus have been found in the northern Gulf of Mexico, the Western Interior Basin of North America, and the Saratov Region of Russia. The animal lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 80 to 75 million years ago. Its time range is the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
Subsequent authors have challenged the placement of L. nichollsae in Latoplatecarpus and reassigned it back to the genus Plioplatecarpus.
